INTRODUCTION · Why we investigate country carbon emission patterns

Emissions kept rising - but not along one shared path

Responsible: SHEN RUITING

3

THE PUZZLE

+63.8%

Sample-wide fossil CO2, 1992 to 2021

21.97 to 35.98 Gt across the 193 countries covered by our panel

30 years

of sustained global climate attention

yet the covered total kept growing - why, and driven by whom?

OUR QUESTION CHAIN

Q1

Is the rise one common trajectory - or different transition pathways?

Q2

Do countries differ only in size, or in speed, timing and fuel mix?

Q3

Can AI identify these pathways stably from trajectory features?

Q4

Where should limited climate-monitoring attention go?

Approach

explore differences → engineer trajectory features → K-means (K = 2) → evaluate separation and stability → pathway-specific monitoring priorities

DESIGN OF AI ALGORITHM · Defining the clustering unit and the modelled cohort

From 213 territories to 193 comparable country profiles

1 / 4

Responsible: RAN CHANGMING

11

COHORT FUNNEL

6,378

country-year rows

OWID backbone + GCB fuel fills, 1992-2021

213

countries & territories

valid ISO codes in the panel

-16

micro states excluded

populations too small for stable trajectories

-4

incomplete histories excluded

fewer than 30 consecutive years 1992-2021

193

modelled countries / entities

complete history + reliable fuel structure

WHY THIS COHORT

Trajectory features need complete histories. Slopes, peaks and post-peak change are only comparable when every country covers the same 30 years.

Fuel features need reliable shares. Entities with unreliable fuel structure would distort the fuel-shift block.

ONE COUNTRY = ONE PROFILE

Each of the 193 countries becomes a single 11-feature trajectory profile - the clustering unit for everything that follows.

AUDITABLE BY DESIGN

Every exclusion is logged with its reason in cohort_audit.csv, so the sample can be reproduced or challenged.

12

DESIGN OF AI ALGORITHM · Turning 30-year emission histories into model features

Eleven features describe level, direction, timing and fuel shift

2 / 4

Responsible: RAN CHANGMING

12

01 · LEVEL

How intense is the economy now?

· Log recent per-capita CO2

· (median 2017-2021)

Log scale stops extreme values from dominating distances.

02 · DIRECTION

Which way is the trajectory moving?

· Long-term log slope 1992-2021

· Recent log slope 2012-2021

· Acceleration (recent - long-term)

Separates long-run direction from recent slowdown or renewed growth.

03 · TIMING

When does change happen?

· Growth volatility (MAD)

· Peak timing (relative)

· Post-peak change

Distinguishes smooth plateauing from unstable or still-rising paths.

04 · FUEL SHIFT

Is the fuel mix decarbonising?

· Recent coal & gas shares

· Coal & gas share change

· (early vs recent 5-yr medians)

Oil share is kept for interpretation but omitted from the model to avoid perfect dependence.

Built only from per-capita CO2, growth rates and fuel shares - total CO2 and population never enter the model; they return later, only to interpret the pathways.

DESIGN OF AI ALGORITHM · Scaling, PCA, K-means and how they are validated

A fixed pipeline turns 30-year histories into two pathways

3 / 4

Responsible: RAN CHANGMING

13

COUNTRY-YEAR PANEL

6,378 rows · 1992-2021

193 COUNTRY PROFILES

one row per country, 11 features

ROBUSTSCALER

median / IQR scaling, so outliers cannot dominate distances

PCA → 4 COMPONENTS

87.41% of variance kept, correlated features merged

K-MEANS · K = 2-8

50 restarts, fixed seed 42: the grouping re-runs identically [4]

VALIDATION RUNS ALONGSIDE - NOT INSIDE - THE CLUSTERING

GMM SOFT MEMBERSHIP

probability of belonging to each cluster

100 x 80% SUBSAMPLING

refit and compare labels (Adjusted Rand Index)

NEITHER CHANGES THE LABELS

both instruments only test the grouping that K-means already produced

WHY K-MEANS

Unsupervised by design: no labels exist for 'transition pathway', so we cluster comparable profiles and validate the structure afterwards.

Simple, explainable, reproducible: a fixed seed and n_init = 50 make the exact grouping re-runnable; PCA removes redundancy among correlated trajectory features before distances are computed.

14

DESIGN OF AI ALGORITHM · Choosing how many emission patterns to keep (K = 2-8)

All three validity metrics rank K = 2 first

4 / 4

Responsible: RAN CHANGMING

14

Inertia (within-cluster sum of squares) always falls as K grows - shown for reference only, never used alone to pick K.

How the decision was made

· Three internal criteria were computed on the same PCA space for every candidate K from 2 to 8, so the comparison is like-for-like. [4] [5]

· All three agree on K = 2; no criterion prefers a finer split, and K = 3-8 lose separation without adding interpretable structure.

· K = 2 is therefore a screening frame for monitoring attention, not a claim that only two kinds of country exist.

0.486 Silhouette

highest - compact, well separated

0.865 Davies-Bouldin

lowest - least overlap

98.3 Calinski-Harabasz

highest - strongest split

DECISION

K = 2 - the strongest macro segmentation, not the most detailed taxonomy.

Highlighted row: K = 2 wins Silhouette, Davies-Bouldin and Calinski-Harabasz simultaneously.

SILHOUETTE

Rewards clusters that are internally compact and well separated from neighbours. [5]

DAVIES-BOULDIN

Penalises overlap between cluster pairs; lower means cleaner separation.

CALINSKI-HARABASZ

Compares between-cluster with within-cluster dispersion; higher is better.

NO SUPERVISED ACCURACY

Accuracy, precision, recall, F1, ROC and confusion matrices require ground-truth labels. Pathways have none - evaluation therefore uses internal validity plus stability.

MODEL EVALUATION AND PERFORMANCE · Resampling stability and membership confidence

The split survives resampling; ten stay uncertain

3 / 3

Responsible: REN SIYU

17

Left: 100 refits on 80% country subsamples - median Adjusted Rand Index 0.965 (minimum 0.778). Right: GMM soft membership on the same feature space. [6]

BOUNDARY COUNTRIES

GMM confidence below 0.70:

South Korea 0.51 · Guatemala 0.53 · Trinidad & Tobago 0.56 · Sri Lanka 0.61 · Estonia 0.63 · Venezuela 0.65 · Oman 0.66 · Jordan 0.66 · Madagascar 0.67 · Azerbaijan 0.68

Not a third pathway - membership to be confirmed with more data.

Verdict: the two-pathway macro structure is stable (ARI close to 1 on most refits), and the only genuine uncertainty is a small, known boundary set - exactly the countries a monitoring programme should track more closely.

WHY ONE LENS FAILS

Rank by emissions only

and you watch China, the US and India while missing small-base, fast-growing, late-peak countries in the upper left.

Rank by growth only

and you overrate small economies while underrating the plateauing majors that hold 92.2% of 2017-21 emissions.

MONITORING PRIORITIES

Rapid-growth pathway (24)

Watch: growth rate · fuel shares · peak timing

Progress = growth slows, high-carbon shares fall

Plateauing pathway (169)

Watch: total emissions · pace of decline

Progress = absolute emissions fall structurally

Boundary countries (10)

Watch: data completeness · membership stability

Progress = pathway membership stabilises with better data

22

CONCLUSIONS · What this investigation changes for climate monitoring

From one emission total to pathway-specific monitoring

Responsible: GROUP 30 - ALL MEMBERS

22

CURRENT BURDEN

The 169-country plateauing pathway holds 92.2% of 2017-2021 sample emissions

Push the plateau into absolute decline - this is the short-term mitigation lever.

FUTURE PRESSURE

The 24-country rapid-growth pathway: fast growth, late peaks, +198% since 1992

Track growth and lock-in signals now, before today's growth becomes tomorrow's burden.

BOUNDARY UNCERTAINTY

10 low-confidence countries identified by soft membership

Observe them more frequently instead of forcing a fixed classification.

What is novel here: an 11-feature trajectory profile (level · direction · timing · fuel shift) that makes 30 years of history comparable per country, and a stability-checked K = 2 screen used as a monitoring tool - not as another league table.

Honest limits: pathways are empirical patterns in 1992-2021, not causes, forecasts or policy verdicts; with no policy or economic variables in the panel, the model prioritises deeper investigation - it does not replace it.

The purpose is not to rank countries, but to identify where different transition pressures require different monitoring priorities.
